tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE.summary: Tau Ceti has built far more of this roadmap than its document records. Lane A's core is done: weak derivatives against Mathlib's `TestFunction` pairing, `W^{k,p}(Ω)` at every order with completeness, `W^{k,p}_0(Ω)`, the Poincaré inequality on `W^{1,p}_0` with explicit constants and a matching counterexample, the `p<n` Sobolev embedding, and Rellich–Kondrachov for `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` on a bounded domain. Lane D is complete end to end — energy form, Gårding, Lax–Milgram existence and uniqueness, the Fredholm alternative, and the Dirichlet spectrum with an eigenfunction Hilbert basis and the Rayleigh principle — and Lane C's maximum principles (weak, strong, Hopf, comparison, and the `c ≥ 0` and bounded-drift extensions) and the `ℝⁿ` Newtonian fundamental solution with `-ΔG = δ₀` are done too; in Lane B the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function with its weak `(1,1)` and strong `(p,p)` inequalities is proved, and so is the diagonal case of Marcinkiewicz interpolation that the document says is not in any library. What is genuinely missing is the trace operator and the general extension operator, Meyers–Serrin for a general domain, the agreement with Mathlib's Bessel-potential scale, Morrey and the borderline embedding, Poincaré–Wirtinger, Calderón–Zygmund and BMO, the `ℝⁿ` mean-value property and Harnack inequality, Green's functions and Perron's method, the whole of Lane E (elliptic regularity: `H²` estimates, `W^{2,p}`, Schauder, De Giorgi–Nash–Moser), and Lane F apart from the semigroup theory, which the OneParameterSemigroups roadmap has already delivered including Hille–Yosida.

targets.target: The weak (distributional) derivative of a locally integrable function on an open set, defined against the test-function pairing
targets.note: `HasWeakLineDerivOn mu Omega u u' v` is exactly `∫ (∂_v φ) • u = -∫ φ • u'` for every bundled test function `φ ∈ 𝓓(Ω,ℝ)` of Mathlib's `Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution/TestFunction.lean`, with local integrability of `u` and `u'` built into the definition; uniqueness a.e. and agreement with the classical derivative are proved. No sorry in the file.

targets.target: `W^{k,p}(Ω)` with its graph norm, for every order `k` and every `1 ≤ p`
targets.note: `Wkp mu Omega p k` is the iterated weak-derivative Sobolev space on an open `Omega` in a finite-dimensional real inner product space with an additive Haar measure; `Wkp … 0 = Lᵖ(Ω)` and `Wkp … 1 = W1p`. The definition records the derivative fields and the theorem `hasWeakFDerivOn_iteratedGradient` checks that consecutive fields really are weak derivatives.

targets.target: Completeness of `W^{k,p}(Ω)`
targets.note: Completeness is proved by the closed-graph argument at every order, sorry-free.

duplicates.note: That milestone asks for `W^{k,p}` of maps of surfaces/strips, i.e. the two-dimensional slice of the same weak-derivative Sobolev spaces, and its own text says it should consume this lane rather than duplicate it.

targets.target: Mollification of weakly differentiable functions (the smoothing step of the density theorem)
targets.note: Convolution with a `ContDiffBump` converges to the identity on `W^{1,p}` and turns a weak derivative into a classical one; the Leibniz/cutoff product rule needed for localisation is proved too.

targets.target: Meyers–Serrin `H = W`: `C^∞ ∩ W^{k,p}(Ω)` is dense in `W^{k,p}(Ω)` for an arbitrary open `Ω`
targets.note: Only the whole-space case is proved: `W^{1,p}_0(ℝⁿ) = W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ)` for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, i.e. density of test functions on `Ω = ⊤`. Meyers–Serrin for a general open `Ω` (and for order `k > 1`) is explicitly disclaimed in the headers of `Wkp/Zero.lean` and `Mollification.lean`; `grep -rn -i 'meyers\|serrin'` finds only those roadmap pointers, no theorem.

targets.target: `W^{k,p}_0(Ω)` as the `C_c^∞(Ω)`-closure
targets.note: Defined at every order as the closure of the range of the embedding `C_c^∞(Ω) → W^{k,p}(Ω)`, with no boundedness or boundary regularity hypothesis; `wkp0Submodule_one` checks that order one agrees with `w1p0Submodule`.

targets.target: `W^{1,p}_0(Ω) ≠ W^{1,p}(Ω)` for bounded `Ω` (the warning that the whole-space equality is special)
targets.note: The ingredient is there — the Poincaré inequality on `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` excludes nonzero constants — and the file headers state the consequence, but no theorem in either library asserts `w1p0Submodule mu Omega p ≠ ⊤` for a nonempty bounded `Omega`.

targets.target: `W^{k,2}(ℝⁿ) = H^{k,2}(ℝⁿ)`: agreement of the weak-derivative scale with Mathlib's Bessel-potential scale
targets.note: Both scales exist — Mathlib's `MemSobolev`/`besselPotential` and Tau Ceti's `Wkp` — but nothing connects them: `grep -rn 'memSobolev\|besselPotential\|MemSobolev' TauCeti/` returns no hit at all, so the two theories are exactly the unrelated pair the layer warns against.

targets.target: The `1 < p < ∞` integer-order Calderón agreement `W^{k,p}(ℝⁿ) = H^{k,p}(ℝⁿ)`
targets.note: Not stated anywhere; it needs the Mihlin–Hörmander/Calderón–Zygmund multiplier theory of Lane B.10, which is itself absent.

targets.target: Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev embedding `W^{1,p} ↪ L^{p*}` for `p < n` (consume)
targets.note: Mathlib proves GNS for compactly supported `C¹` functions; Tau Ceti transfers it to the closure and bundles `W^{1,p}_0(Ω) →L[ℝ] L^{p⋆}(Ω)`. The transfer is only on `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)`, which is the honest form: the estimate `‖u‖_{p⋆} ≤ C‖∇u‖_p` fails on all of `W^{1,p}(Ω)` (constants).

targets.target: Morrey embedding `W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪ C^{0,1−n/p}(Ω)` for `p > n`
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'morrey'` over both trees finds only Mathlib's Rademacher file (which credits Morrey's proof of a different theorem) and Tau Ceti's own disclaimer in `Embedding.lean` that the `p > n` regime is not proved here.

targets.target: The borderline `p = n` embedding (BMO / exponential integrability, Trudinger–Moser)
targets.note: Neither stated nor proved; BMO itself does not exist in either library (see milestone B.11).

targets.target: Poincaré inequality on `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` for bounded `Ω`, with explicit constant
targets.note: Proved with the explicit constant `b - a` (the slab width), under the weaker hypothesis that `Ω` is bounded in one direction, so it is more general than the stated bounded-`Ω` form; the ball corollary gives the constant `2R`. The companion counterexample shows no constant works on `ℝⁿ`, so the side condition is known to be load-bearing.

targets.target: Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality (zero mean) with explicit constant dependence
targets.note: Only the pointwise Riesz-potential estimate behind it (Gilbarg–Trudinger Lemma 7.16) is proved: `‖u x - ⨍_S u‖ ≤ D^n/(n μ S) ∫ ‖Du y‖ ‖x-y‖^{1-n}`. The `Lᵖ` bound on the Riesz potential, and hence the Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality itself, is not proved; `Poincare/W1p0.lean` says so explicitly.

targets.target: Trace operator `W^{1,p}(Ω) → L^p(∂Ω)` for Lipschitz `∂Ω`
targets.note: Nothing in either tree: the only hits for a Sobolev trace are the three places where Tau Ceti's files note that they deliberately avoid needing one (`W1p/Zero.lean`, `PDE/DirichletProblem.lean`). Mathlib's `trace` is the linear-algebra/field trace.

targets.target: `ker(trace) = W^{1,p}_0(Ω)`
targets.note: Cannot be stated without the trace operator; absent.

targets.target: Extension operator `W^{1,p}(Ω) → W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ)`
targets.note: Only extension by zero out of `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` is built (an isometry onto its image, needing no boundary regularity). A bounded extension operator defined on all of `W^{1,p}(Ω)` — the statement that actually needs Lipschitz `∂Ω` — is absent.

targets.target: Rellich–Kondrachov: `W^{1,p}(Ω) ↪↪ L^p(Ω)` compact for bounded `Ω`
targets.note: Compactness of `W^{1,p}_0(Ω) → Lᵖ(Ω)` is proved for `1 ≤ p < ∞` and bounded `Ω` with no boundary regularity, via the Fréchet–Kolmogorov criterion, which Tau Ceti also proves. This is the form Lane D consumes; the statement for the full `W^{1,p}(Ω)`, which needs the missing extension operator, is explicitly not claimed.

duplicates.note: Also asks for the trace on Sobolev spaces of maps of surfaces/strips, the two-dimensional case of the trace operator here.

targets.target: The Hölder space `C^{0,α}` as a Banach space
targets.note: Bounded continuous globally `α`-Hölder maps with the norm `‖f‖_∞ + [f]_α`, complete when the codomain is; built on Mathlib's `MemHolder`/`nnHolderNorm`.

targets.target: The Hölder space `C^{1,α}` as a Banach space
targets.note: Bounded `C¹` maps with bounded globally `α`-Hölder derivative, Banach when the codomain is.

targets.target: The whole scale `C^{k,α}(Ω)` as Banach spaces, in particular `C^{2,α}` (the Schauder target)
targets.note: Only orders `k = 0` and `k = 1` are constructed; there is no `C^{k,α}` for general `k` and in particular no `C^{2,α}`, which is the space the Schauder estimates of Lane E.22 are stated in. The spaces built are also the *global* ones on a metric space rather than domain-relative `C^{k,α}(Ω)` spaces.

targets.target: Weak derivatives and `W^{k,p}(Ω)` with completeness (item 1)
targets.note: Fully built on Mathlib's `TestFunction` pairing, exactly as the layer prescribes.

targets.target: Density, Meyers–Serrin and `W^{k,p}_0` (item 2)
targets.note: `W^{k,p}_0` is defined at every order and density of test functions is proved on `ℝⁿ`; Meyers–Serrin `H = W` for a general domain is not.

targets.target: Agreement with the Bessel-potential scale (item 3)
targets.note: Nothing in Tau Ceti mentions `memSobolev` or `besselPotential`.

targets.target: Embeddings: GNS, Morrey, borderline (item 4)
targets.note: Subcritical `p < n` is done; Morrey `p > n` and the borderline `p = n` are absent.

targets.target: Poincaré and Poincaré–Wirtinger (item 5)
targets.note: Poincaré on `W^{1,p}_0` is proved with explicit constants and a matching counterexample; Poincaré–Wirtinger stops at the potential estimate.

targets.target: Trace, extension, Rellich (item 6)
targets.note: Rellich–Kondrachov holds on `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)`; the trace operator and the general extension operator are absent.

targets.target: Hölder spaces `C^{k,α}(Ω)` as Banach spaces (item 7)
targets.note: Orders 0 and 1 only.

duplicates.note: That lane needs the two-dimensional slice of exactly this package (`W^{k,p}`, Sobolev multiplication, trace, Calderón–Zygmund) and its own text directs it to consume this lane.

targets.target: The Hardy–Littlewood maximal function `Mf`
targets.note: The centred maximal function `M f x = ⨆ r > 0, ⨍⁻ ball x r ‖f‖ₑ` on a metric measure space, with sublinearity, lower semicontinuity and measurability.

targets.target: The weak `(1,1)` maximal inequality, via Vitali covering
targets.note: `t * μ {M f > t} ≤ 4^n ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ` for an additive Haar measure on a real normed space of dimension `n`, proved from Mathlib's `Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall` exactly as the layer asks.

targets.target: The strong `(p,p)` maximal inequality for `p > 1`
targets.note: With an explicit constant, obtained by Marcinkiewicz interpolation between the weak `(1,1)` bound and the `L^∞` endpoint.

targets.target: The Lebesgue differentiation theorem as a corollary
targets.note: Mathlib proves Lebesgue differentiation for any Vitali family and any locally integrable `f`, which is more general than the ball form the layer wants as a corollary.

targets.target: Marcinkiewicz interpolation (weak type to strong type)
targets.note: Only the diagonal endpoint case `p₀ = 1, p₁ = ∞` is proved: a sublinear operator of weak type `(1,1)` and bounded on `L^∞` is bounded on every `Lᵖ`, `1 < p < ∞`, with an explicit constant. The general `(p₀,q₀),(p₁,q₁)` Marcinkiewicz theorem (off-diagonal, `q ≠ p`) is not proved.

targets.target: Riesz–Thorin complex interpolation
targets.note: Absent: `grep -rn -i 'riesz.thorin'` over both trees returns nothing. Mathlib has the Hadamard three-lines theorem, the complex-analytic input to Riesz–Thorin, but no interpolation theorem for operators.

targets.target: The Calderón–Zygmund decomposition of an `L¹` function at height `t`
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'calder\|zygmund'` over both trees finds only Tau Ceti's roadmap pointers in `MaximalFunction.lean` and `Marcinkiewicz.lean` and a reference to Stein's book title; no decomposition theorem.

targets.target: Calderón–Zygmund singular integral operators with standard kernel bounds, bounded on `Lᵖ` for `1 < p < ∞` and weak-`(1,1)`
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'singular integral'` finds only bibliography entries. No notion of a CZ kernel exists.

targets.target: The Mihlin–Hörmander multiplier theorem
targets.note: Mathlib has the `FourierMultiplier` machinery the layer says to consume, but no boundedness theorem for multipliers satisfying Mihlin–Hörmander derivative bounds; `grep -rn -i 'mihlin'` returns nothing.

duplicates.note: Asks for the Calderón–Zygmund inequality `‖u‖_{W^{1,p}} ≤ C‖∂̄u‖_{L^p}` via the Cauchy kernel, i.e. the two-dimensional ∂̄ case of the same singular-integral bound.

targets.target: The space `BMO(ℝⁿ)` of functions of bounded mean oscillation
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'bounded mean oscillation'` over both trees returns nothing; the only `BMO` matches are the local hypothesis name `Bmo` in Mathlib's cyclotomic polynomial file.

targets.target: The John–Nirenberg inequality
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'john.nirenberg'` returns nothing.

targets.target: The `L^∞ → BMO` endpoint for Calderón–Zygmund operators
targets.note: Both sides of the statement are missing.

targets.target: Hardy–Littlewood maximal function and the maximal inequality (item 8)
targets.note: Fully built, including the Lebesgue differentiation corollary which Mathlib already has in Vitali-family generality.

targets.target: Interpolation: Marcinkiewicz and Riesz–Thorin (item 9)
targets.note: Contrary to the roadmap text, the diagonal `(1,1)`–`(∞,∞)` case of Marcinkiewicz *is* in Tau Ceti; the general Marcinkiewicz theorem and Riesz–Thorin are not.

targets.target: Calderón–Zygmund decomposition, singular integral operators, Mihlin–Hörmander (item 10)
targets.note: Nothing at all.

targets.target: BMO and John–Nirenberg (item 11)
targets.note: Nothing at all.

duplicates.note: Its item 2 is the ∂̄ Calderón–Zygmund inequality, the two-dimensional slice of item 10 here.

targets.target: The mean-value property of harmonic functions on `ℝⁿ` (sphere/ball averages), and its converse characterization
targets.note: Only `n = 2`: Mathlib's mean-value property is for `f : ℂ → F` and uses `circleAverage`. There is no sphere or ball average characterization of `InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd` on a general finite-dimensional real inner product space, and no converse. Tau Ceti has only the translation/dilation invariance lemmas that such a proof would normalise with.

targets.target: Smoothness (`C^∞`/analyticity) of harmonic functions on `ℝⁿ`
targets.note: `HarmonicAt.analyticAt` is again the planar case, proved through `Re` of a holomorphic function. In general dimension `HarmonicOnNhd.contDiffOn` only returns the `C²` regularity that is part of the definition of `HarmonicAt`, so the genuine smoothness theorem on `ℝⁿ` is missing.

targets.target: The weak maximum principle for `Δ` (subharmonic functions bounded by their boundary values)
targets.note: Continuous on a compact `K`, `C²` and `0 ≤ Δ f` on `interior K` implies the bound on `K` from any bound on `frontier K`, in any finite-dimensional real inner product space.

targets.target: The strong maximum principle for `Δ`
targets.note: Proved in every dimension on a preconnected open set, via Hopf's lemma (so without needing a mean-value property); the planar harmonic version is proved separately from Harnack.

targets.target: The Hopf boundary-point lemma
targets.note: The classical barrier proof, in every dimension, for subharmonic functions on a ball.

targets.target: The comparison principle
targets.note: Both the weak comparison principle and Dirichlet uniqueness for the Poisson equation, plus the strong comparison principle.

targets.target: The maximum principle for a general elliptic `L` with sign condition `c ≥ 0`
targets.note: Proved for `-Δ - b·∇ + c` with bounded drift `b` and `c ≥ 0`, together with the counterexample showing `c ≥ 0` is necessary. The principal part is still the Laplacian: no weak maximum principle is proved for a variable principal coefficient `aⁱʲ(x)`, and there is no strong maximum principle or Hopf lemma for lower-order or variable-coefficient `L`.

targets.target: The Harnack inequality for nonnegative harmonic functions
targets.note: Proved only in the plane, on a disk, with the sharp constant `((R+r)/(R-r))²`, by the Poisson-kernel argument (Mathlib's `circleAverage_poissonKernel_smul`). The `ℝⁿ` Harnack inequality for nonnegative harmonic functions is absent — the proof would need the `n`-dimensional Poisson kernel or mean-value property of C.12, neither of which exists.

targets.target: The Harnack inequality for a general elliptic `L`
targets.note: Absent; this is the De Giorgi–Nash–Moser-level statement of Lane E.23 and nothing in either library approaches it.

duplicates.note: E.23 asks for the elliptic Harnack inequality for divergence-form operators with bounded measurable coefficients, the general-`L` half of this milestone.

targets.target: The fundamental solution / Newtonian potential of `Δ` on `ℝⁿ`
targets.note: For `n ≥ 3` the normalised kernel `(n(n-2)ω_n)^{-1}‖x‖^{2-n}` is defined and the distributional identity `-ΔG = δ₀` is proved (`∫ Δf · G = -f 0` for compactly supported `C²` `f`), with the pole at an arbitrary point. The planar logarithmic kernel is defined and is harmonic off the pole, but its distributional identity is explicitly left open.

targets.target: The Green's function on the ball/half-space
targets.note: `grep -rn -i "green's function\|greensFunction\|greenFunction"` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: The Poisson kernel on the ball/half-space
targets.note: Only the planar disk: Mathlib's Poisson/Herglotz–Riesz kernel reproduces a harmonic function on a disk from its boundary values. No `ℝⁿ` ball or half-space Poisson kernel.

targets.target: Perron's method and solvability of the Dirichlet problem `Δu = 0`, `u = g` on `∂Ω`, with barriers at regular boundary points
targets.note: Absent. There is no subharmonic-function class (Tau Ceti's 'subharmonic' occurrences are the inline hypothesis `0 ≤ Δ f` in the maximum-principle files), no Perron envelope and no barrier notion. Only uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem is proved (`TauCeti.eqOn_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_eqOn_frontier`), not existence.

targets.target: Mean-value property and smoothness of harmonic functions on `ℝⁿ` (item 12)
targets.note: The `n = 2` theory the layer says to consume is in Mathlib; the `ℝⁿ` generalisation it asks to build is absent.

targets.target: Weak and strong maximum principles, Hopf lemma, comparison principle (item 13)
targets.note: Essentially complete for `Δ` and for `-Δ - b·∇ + c` with `c ≥ 0`; only a variable principal coefficient `aⁱʲ` is missing.

targets.target: The Harnack inequality (item 14)
targets.note: Planar disk only.

targets.target: Fundamental solution, Green's function, Poisson kernel, Perron's method (item 15)
targets.note: The Newtonian fundamental solution on `ℝⁿ` (`n ≥ 3`) is done including `-ΔG = δ₀`; Green's function, the `ℝⁿ` Poisson kernel and Perron's method are absent.

targets.target: Uniform ellipticity with explicit constants `0 < λ ≤ Λ`
targets.note: `UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam` carries the two-sided bound with `λ, Λ` as explicit parameters, exactly the named definition the roadmap asks for.

targets.target: The energy bilinear form `a(u,v) = ∫ aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu ∂ⱼv + bⁱ ∂ᵢu v + c u v` on `H¹(Ω)` and `H¹₀(Ω)`
targets.note: Built on `TauCeti.W1p`/`W1p0` with `p = 2`, with bilinearity and symmetry for symmetric principal coefficients and zero drift.

targets.target: Boundedness of the energy form
targets.note: With an explicit constant `Λ + β + γ` from the coefficient bounds.

targets.target: Gårding's inequality `a(u,u) ≥ α‖u‖²_{H¹} − β‖u‖²_{L²}` from uniform ellipticity
targets.note: `garding_energyFormH1_self_norm` is literally the roadmap's form `(λ/2)‖u‖²_{H¹} − (λ/2 + β²/2λ)‖u‖²_{L²} ≤ a(u,u)`, for bounded measurable coefficients with `c ≥ 0`.

targets.target: Lax–Milgram (consume)
targets.note: Mathlib has Lax–Milgram; Tau Ceti adds the variational `∃!` form that the Dirichlet theorem consumes.

targets.target: The weak formulation of the Dirichlet problem and its forcing functional
targets.note: `u ∈ H¹₀(Ω)` with `a(u,v) = ∫_Ω f v` for all `v ∈ H¹₀(Ω)`; the boundary condition is membership in `H¹₀(Ω)`, so no trace operator is needed.

targets.target: Existence and uniqueness of the weak solution when `a` is coercive
targets.note: The end-to-end theorem is there, with concrete coercivity hypotheses supplied from uniform ellipticity plus a slab or ball containing `Ω`, and the `-Δu = f` in a ball payoff named separately. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Compactness of the resolvent from Rellich
targets.note: The `L²` mass form represented relative to the coercive energy form is a compact operator on `H¹₀(Ω)` for bounded `Ω`, exactly the Rellich input the layer names.

targets.target: The Fredholm alternative for `Lu = f` (unique solution, or finite-dimensional kernel)
targets.note: The dichotomy is proved for the mass-shifted weak equation `B(u,v) - κ⟪u,v⟫_{L²} = ⟪f,v⟫_{L²}`, which is the standard reduction of a Gårding form to a coercive one; the homogeneous solution space is finite dimensional. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Dirichlet eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of `−Δ` (and of a general divergence-form `L`) on a bounded `Ω`
targets.note: Defined for the general divergence-form operator, hence more general than `−Δ`; every eigenvalue is positive and bounded below by the coercivity constant, with the explicit `1/(2(4R²+1))` bound for a domain in a ball of radius `R`.

targets.target: A compact self-adjoint inverse (Rellich plus Lax–Milgram)
targets.note: The solution operator on `L²(Ω)` is compact for bounded `Ω`, symmetric when the energy form is, and positive.

targets.target: The eigenfunction basis from the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
targets.note: An orthonormal basis of `L²(Ω)` of Dirichlet eigenfunctions, in which the Dirichlet problem is solved by eigenfunction expansion; eigenspaces are finite dimensional.

targets.target: The variational (Rayleigh) characterization of the first eigenvalue
targets.note: The first eigenvalue is attained on a nonempty bounded domain and equals the optimal Poincaré constant, matching the roadmap's acceptance criterion. The parenthetical 'Sturm–Liouville / separation-of-variables payoff' is not itself formalised: `grep -rn -i 'sturm.liouville'` finds nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Weak formulation, boundedness, Gårding (item 16)
targets.note: All three parts proved for bounded measurable coefficients.

targets.target: Existence and uniqueness in the coercive case (item 17)
targets.note: Consumes Mathlib's Lax–Milgram as the layer prescribes.

targets.target: The Fredholm alternative in the non-coercive case (item 18)
targets.note: Uses Rellich to make the mass operator compact, as specified.

targets.target: Spectrum of `−Δ` (item 19)
targets.note: Eigenvalues, eigenfunction basis and the Rayleigh principle, for general divergence-form `L` and hence for `−Δ`.

targets.target: Difference-quotient machinery for weak derivatives
targets.note: No difference-quotient characterization of Sobolev membership exists; Tau Ceti's `Sobolev/Translation.lean` proves only the one-sided estimate `‖u(·+h) - u‖_p ≤ ‖h‖‖∇u‖_p`, not its converse, which is the tool this milestone needs.

targets.target: Interior `H²` regularity: a weak `H¹` solution with `L²` data is locally `H²`
targets.note: Absent from both trees; nothing relates `IsWeakSolutionDirichlet` to membership in `Wkp … 2`.

targets.target: `Hᵏ` bootstrapping to `C^∞` for smooth coefficients and data
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: `Lᵖ` theory of `D²u` for `Δu = f` (the Calderón–Zygmund `W^{2,p}` estimate)
targets.note: Absent; it depends on Lane B.10, which is itself absent.

targets.target: `W^{2,p}` estimates for variable continuous/VMO coefficients
targets.note: Absent; VMO does not exist in either library (`grep -rn -i 'vmo\|vanishing mean oscillation'` finds nothing).

duplicates.note: Asks for the Calderón–Zygmund inequality and interior elliptic bootstrapping for the ∂̄ operator, the same estimate in the two-dimensional first-order case.

targets.target: Interior and global `C^{2,α}` Schauder estimates for `C^{0,α}` coefficients
targets.note: Absent. Only the `C^{0,α}` and `C^{1,α}` target spaces exist; `C^{2,α}` does not, and no estimate is proved. `grep -rn -i 'schauder'` finds only Mathlib's Schauder *bases* and Tau Ceti's roadmap pointers.

targets.target: Campanato/Morrey space characterization
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'campanato'` returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Classical solvability of the Dirichlet problem in `C^{2,α}`
targets.note: Absent; only the weak `H¹₀` solvability of Lane D exists.

targets.target: Local boundedness of weak solutions of divergence-form equations with bounded measurable coefficients
targets.note: Absent; `grep -rn -i 'de giorgi\|moser iteration\|nash.moser'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Hölder continuity of weak solutions (De Giorgi–Nash–Moser)
targets.note: The weak-solution predicate exists and the energy form is stated exactly for bounded measurable coefficients, so the statement is expressible, but no regularity theorem is proved.

targets.target: The elliptic Harnack inequality for bounded measurable coefficients
targets.note: Only the planar harmonic Harnack inequality exists; the divergence-form version is absent.

duplicates.note: C.14 asks for the Harnack inequality 'then for general elliptic L', which is the same statement as the elliptic Harnack inequality named here.

targets.target: Interior `H²`/`Hᵏ` estimates via difference quotients (item 20)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Calderón–Zygmund `W^{2,p}` estimates (item 21)
targets.note: Absent, and its Lane B input is absent too.

targets.target: Schauder `C^{2,α}` estimates (item 22)
targets.note: Absent; even the `C^{2,α}` target space is missing.

targets.target: De Giorgi–Nash–Moser (item 23)
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Item 2 of that lane is interior elliptic bootstrapping and boundary regularity for the ∂̄ operator, the two-dimensional first-order counterpart of this lane's regularity theory.

targets.note: Mathlib's `Lp V p μ` is the Bochner `Lᵖ` space for any `NormedAddCommGroup V`, so `L²(0,T;V)` is `Lp V 2 (volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 T))` and is complete for complete `V`. What is missing is any dedicated API for the time interval; nothing in either tree is written for it.

targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti's `Wkp` is a scalar-valued space on a domain in a finite-dimensional inner product space; there is no Banach-valued Sobolev space in one time variable.

targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'gelfand triple'` over both trees returns nothing; Mathlib's `Gelfand` material is the commutative-Banach-algebra transform.

targets.note: Absent.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability.summary: This roadmap is essentially finished in Tau Ceti, and the summary at its head — that Mathlib does not carry the exchangeability theory — is now out of date about the library as a whole. `TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability/` and `TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti/` contain the symmetry predicates and their implication lattice, the path-law bridges, process tails and the strict chain `invariants (shift α) < pathTail α < exchangeableSigma α`, Hewitt–Savage, the product-kernel adapters and both common endings, the whole L² averaging library, reverse martingales with `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf`, the Koopman/mean-ergodic lane with the projection identified as conditional expectation, and the directing-measure theory: `deFinetti`, `deFinetti_viaL2`, `deFinetti_viaKoopman`, the Ryll-Nardzewski equivalence, a.e. uniqueness of the directing measure, the full-path joint disintegration, empirical-measure convergence in both the topology-free and Polish forms, and the zero-one / ergodic / extreme-point interfaces — all sorry-free, with the roadmap's own milestone names. Layer 8 is largely done too: the finite de Finetti bound with its sampling API, de Finetti for countable index types, the affine barycenter correspondence, and the full Diaconis–Freedman theorem for Markov exchangeability. The one genuine gap is the converse direction of Aldous–Hoover: the array subtree proves that codings are exchangeable and dissociated, but not that every exchangeable array admits such a coding.

targets.target: The symmetry predicates `Exchangeable`, `FullyExchangeable`, `ExchangeableAt n`, `Contractable`
targets.note: All four are defined exactly as the layer specifies, in the single `Contractable` API the roadmap commits to; no `Spreadable` duplicate exists.

targets.target: `pathLaw μ X`, prefix projections and prefix cylinders
targets.note: Block, prefix and path laws with their projection compatibilities.

targets.target: `measure_eq_of_fin_marginals_eq`: a `ℕ`-prefix wrapper over Mathlib's projective-limit uniqueness
targets.note: Exactly the wrapper the layer describes, over Mathlib's `IsProjectiveLimit.unique`, with the `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` hypothesis the layer prescribes.

targets.target: Finite approximation of infinite permutations and extension of strictly monotone finite selections to permutations
targets.note: Named `exists_strictMono_nat_extending_fin` / `Finset.exists_perm_eqOn_le_apply` rather than the roadmap's `exists_perm_extending_strictMono`, but the content is the layer's.

targets.target: `contractable_of_exchangeable` and the `Contractable` pushforward API
targets.note: The roadmap's `contractable_of_exchangeable` is `Exchangeable.contractable`; the other three names are literal.

targets.target: `exchangeable_iff_fullyExchangeable` and the adjacent-transposition characterization
targets.note: The adjacent-transposition reduction is stated finite-dimensionally for `ExchangeableAt`, as the layer requires, not for `FullyExchangeable`.

targets.target: Contractability via the monoid of strictly increasing maps `ℕ → ℕ`
targets.note: Both the process-level and the path-law-level characterizations.

targets.target: Mixtures of i.i.d. laws are exchangeable, and exchangeable laws are stationary
targets.note: Stationarity is proved in the sharper form that the path law is shift-invariant, and already for the weaker hypothesis `Contractable`.

targets.target: The implication lattice among `ExchangeableAt n`, `Exchangeable`, `FullyExchangeable`, `Contractable`, `MixedIID`, `ConditionallyIID`
targets.note: Every easy arrow is named and the hard arrow `Contractable → ConditionallyIID` is isolated as `conditionallyIID_of_contractable` in `DeFinetti/Theorem.lean`, exactly the layering the roadmap asks for.

targets.target: The process-level ↔ path-law bridges in both directions
targets.note: Both viewpoints exist with `iff` bridges, which is precisely what the layer's API warning demands.

targets.target: Measurability of the random product kernel `ω ↦ (ν ω)^{⊗ Fin m}`
targets.note: Both the finite `Fin m` product and the countable power `P ↦ P^{⊗ℕ}` are measurable as maps of probability measures.

targets.target: Measurability of the joint kernel `ω ↦ δ_{ν ω} ⊗ (ν ω)^{⊗m}` and its AE version
targets.note: Exactly the measurability the layer says `Measure.bind_apply` needs, in both the measurable and a.e.-measurable forms.

targets.target: Rectangle evaluation and equality-from-rectangles for random product measures
targets.note: Specialised to the random product measures, on top of Mathlib's `isPiSystem_pi`/`generateFrom_pi` as the layer prescribes.

targets.target: `mixedIID_of_mixingRepresentative`: the mixture common ending
targets.note: Literal name, with the indicator-product factorization hypothesis over finite injective selections that the layer describes.

targets.target: `conditionallyIID_of_jointRectangles`: the joint-rectangle strengthening
targets.note: The common conditional ending is shared by the L² and Koopman routes exactly as the layer plans; `…_of_measure_inter_blockCylinder_eq_setLIntegral` is the variant the Koopman route calls.

targets.target: Process-relative tails: `tailFamily`, `tailProcess`, antitonicity and the comparisons
targets.note: All five milestone names are literal.

targets.target: `tailProcess_eq_iInf_revFiltration`
targets.note: Literal; it is what lets the Layer 4 antitone martingale limit be identified with a conditional expectation given the process tail.

targets.target: The path-space shift and its measurable iterates
targets.note: Both the path-space shift and the process-level shift, with the compatibility `processShift_eq_shift_iterate`.

targets.target: The shift-invariant σ-algebra, consumed from Mathlib rather than re-aliased
targets.note: Tau Ceti uses `MeasurableSpace.invariants (shift α)` directly and introduces no shift-specialised aliases, exactly as the layer directs; only the genuinely new comparison results are stated.

targets.target: The exchangeable σ-algebra, `exchangeableSigma_le`, and its relation to the tail
targets.note: The roadmap's `tail_le_exchangeableSigma` is `pathTail_le_exchangeableSigma`, and Tau Ceti goes further: the strict chain `invariants (shift α) < pathTail α < exchangeableSigma α` is proved over `Bool`, so the layer's warning against identifying the two σ-algebras is discharged by theorem.

targets.target: The measurability target for a directing measure with respect to the tail σ-algebra
targets.note: Both the tail-measurable directing measure of the martingale/L² routes and the invariant-measurable conditional law of the Koopman route.

targets.target: The Hewitt–Savage zero-one law
targets.note: Literal name; the symmetric σ-algebra is trivial for an i.i.d. sequence, with the identically-distributed hypothesis carried explicitly as the layer requires.

targets.target: Equality of means/integrals and of pair covariances from equal low-dimensional laws, and the uniform covariance structure of a contractable L² sequence
targets.note: Literal milestone name; the one- and two-dimensional transfer lemmas are the supporting results in the same file.

targets.target: Two-window L² bounds for block averages, and long-average versus tail-average bounds
targets.note: Both literal milestone names.

targets.target: L¹ convergence of bounded-observable block averages along eventually injective moving selections
targets.note: Literal, with an `MemLp` generalisation.

targets.target: Tail measurability of the limit and its identification with `μ[f ∘ X 0 | tailProcess X]`
targets.note: Literal milestone names.

targets.target: Identification of the indicator limit with the evaluation of the canonical tail conditional law
targets.note: Uses the canonical `directingMeasure` (the conditional law of `X 0` given `tailProcess X`) rather than reconstructing a second measure, exactly as the layer insists.

targets.target: Simultaneous L¹ convergence of finite products along disjoint windows, and the tail-conditioned block factorization
targets.note: Both literal milestone names.

targets.target: `conditionallyIIDWith_directingProbabilityMeasure`, `conditionallyIID_of_contractable_viaL2`, `deFinetti_viaL2` and the Ryll-Nardzewski equivalence
targets.note: The route ends at the standard-Borel conditional theorem, not a relabelled real-valued result, and it is independent of the reverse-martingale files at the import level.

duplicates.note: Layer 6 states the same summit (`conditionallyIID_of_contractable`, `deFinetti`, the Ryll-Nardzewski equivalence) by the martingale route; the roadmap keeps the two as deliberately independent proofs with suffixed names.

targets.target: Finite-horizon reversal: `revFiltration`, `revCEFinite`, `revCEFinite_martingale`
targets.note: Literal milestone names, in the `MeasureTheory` namespace (they are ordinary martingale theory with no exchangeability, which is where the roadmap says they belong).

targets.target: The antitone adapter for Mathlib's upcrossing bound
targets.note: Literal; only the adapter is new, the crossing counts are Mathlib's as the layer intends.

targets.target: Existence of the a.e. limit of `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` along an antitone filtration
targets.note: Literal milestone name.

targets.target: Identification of the limit: `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf`
targets.note: The roadmap's target theorem, with exactly its hypotheses (`[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`, antitone `𝔽`, `𝔽 0 ≤ ⊤`, integrable `f`); `ae_limit_is_condexp_iInf` is the file's `condExp_iInf_ae_eq_of_tendsto_ae_of_tendsto_eLpNorm`. It is stated with no exchangeability, as the layer requires.

targets.target: The L¹/Lᵖ convergence forms
targets.note: The follow-up targets of the layer: `eLpNorm` (hence L¹) convergence of `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` to `μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]`.

targets.target: The Koopman/composition operator on `Lᵖ` for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, an isometric embedding
targets.note: Mathlib supplies the operator and its isometry; Tau Ceti adds the bridge between the operator-level and pointwise Birkhoff averages. The layer's own instruction is to state it at this generality rather than only on `L²`, and that is what is there.

targets.target: The Markov operator on measurable germs / `L^∞`: positive, unital and (for the deterministic Koopman operator) multiplicative
targets.note: `koopmanMarkov_mul` is the multiplicativity the layer singles out as special to composition operators.

targets.target: `fixedSpace`, the mean ergodic projection `metProjection`, and `birkhoffAverage_tendsto_metProjection`
targets.note: All four are literal milestone names.

targets.target: Identification of the projection with conditional expectation onto the invariant σ-algebra
targets.note: This is the roadmap's `proj_eq_condexp` / `lpMeas_eq_fixedSubspace` pair, and the file header explicitly flags it as a separate theorem rather than a simp step, exactly the layer's warning.

targets.target: Path-space specialisation: shift preservation from contractability and the shift-invariant conditional law
targets.note: The roadmap's `pathSpace_shift_preserving_of_contractable` / `measure_map_shift_eq_of_contractable` are `ContractableLaw.measurePreserving_shift` and `Contractable.map_shift_iterate_pathLaw`; `metProjectionShift`/`condexpL2` are covered by the generic `metProjection` results instantiated at the shift.

targets.target: `deFinetti_viaKoopman` and the conditional-i.i.d. transfer
targets.note: The Koopman route reaches the summit and is import-independent of the L² route; `conditionallyIID_transfer` is `ConditionallyIIDWith.of_pathLaw`, which carries the path-space statement to an arbitrary sample space.

targets.target: Kallenberg's contraction-independence lemma and the future/tail filtration comparison
targets.note: The contraction-independence step and the passage from the future filtration to `tailProcess X` by `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf` are both proved.

targets.target: Construction of the directing measure from tail conditional laws
targets.note: A genuine API, not just an existence proof: the witness is named, bundled as a `ProbabilityMeasure`, and characterised by conditional expectation.

targets.target: Finite-product factorization and the summit theorems `conditionallyIID_of_contractable`, `conditionallyIID_of_exchangeable`, `deFinetti`
targets.note: `deFinetti` concludes `ConditionallyIID` over a nonempty standard Borel state space, the sharp Kallenberg 1.1 form the layer demands as the summit.

targets.target: `deFinetti_equivalence`, `deFinetti_RyllNardzewski_equivalence` and `mixedIID_of_contractable`
targets.note: The mixture forms are retained as integrated-out corollaries, never as the summit, exactly as the layer specifies.

targets.target: a.e. uniqueness of the directing measure among `ConditionallyIIDWith` witnesses, and uniqueness of the mixing law
targets.note: Both literal, and the roadmap's warning is respected: the witness-level a.e. uniqueness is stated only for `ConditionallyIIDWith`, while for `MixedIIDWith` only the mixing law `μ.map ν` is shown unique, under `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`.

targets.target: The full-path joint disintegration `μ.map (ω ↦ (ν ω, X · ω)) = iidMixtureLaw (μ.map ν) id`
targets.note: Literal name and literal statement.

targets.target: Empirical tests and frequencies without a topology on the state space
targets.note: All three requested names exist, including the one-null-set-per-countable-family form.

targets.target: Weak empirical-measure convergence on a Polish state space
targets.note: Both literal, with the `[PolishSpace α] [BorelSpace α]` hypotheses the layer prescribes.

targets.target: The mixture-of-product-measures form with the unique law of the directing measure
targets.note: `pathLaw μ X = ∫ P^{⊗ℕ} dπ(P)` with a unique `π`.

targets.target: The zero-one, ergodic and extreme interfaces for exchangeable laws
targets.note: All three interfaces are proved with the roadmap's own names, including the `ErgodicSMul` form for the finitely supported permutation action (Mathlib's `ErgodicSMul`), which the layer flags as a genuine API lemma rather than plumbing.

duplicates.note: Layer 3 reaches the same conditional summit by the L² route; the suffixed `…_viaL2` names are deliberate parallel proofs of the theorems stated here.
Layer 5 reaches the same summit by the Koopman route (`deFinetti_viaKoopman`).

targets.target: Curated export modules `TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability.lean` and `TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti.lean`
targets.note: Both re-export modules exist in the baseline at the suggested paths and declare nothing of their own; a worked example lives at `TauCeti/Examples/Probability/DeFinetti.lean`. This layer is packaging, not mathematics.

targets.target: Every name on the export list
targets.note: Each of the roughly thirty identifiers the layer lists was looked up in the baseline index and found, with the route suffixes kept and the unsuffixed `deFinetti` being the martingale route, exactly as the layer directs.

targets.target: `empiricalMeasureOfFintype` for a finite population, with evaluation, integration and measurability, and `empiricalMeasure` as its `Fin (n+1)` specialization
targets.note: One shared finite-sum construction, with the sequence-specific `empiricalMeasure` defined from it, as the layer requires.

targets.target: `sampleWithoutReplacement`, `sampleWithReplacement`, and their identification with the empirical-measure mixture
targets.note: All literal milestone names.

targets.target: The finite de Finetti bound: two-sided comparison of `prefixLaw μ X m` with `sampleWithReplacement (prefixLaw μ X n)` with error `(m choose 2)/n`
targets.note: Both eventwise inequalities are proved, in the convention-free form the layer demands rather than as a bare total-variation statement.

targets.target: de Finetti for other countable index types
targets.note: The theorem is transported along an equivalence with `ℕ`, giving it for every countably infinite index type.

targets.target: The affine and ergodic decomposition: `p ↦ p^{⊗ℕ}` and the de Finetti barycenter as an affine correspondence, with the components identified as the ergodic ones
targets.note: The barycenter, the affine bijection with exchangeable path laws, its restriction to point masses, and the identification of the components with the extreme — equivalently ergodic, by the Layer 6 `ErgodicSMul` interface — laws.

targets.target: Markov exchangeability and the Diaconis–Freedman representation
targets.note: The full Diaconis–Freedman theorem is proved: a recurrent Markov exchangeable process that attains every state is a mixture of Markov chains, together with the excursion-mixture decomposition and the easy converse `MixedMarkovChain.markovExchangeable`.

targets.target: Exchangeable arrays and the Aldous–Hoover representation
targets.note: A large array subtree exists — separate/joint exchangeability, dissociation, the corner-tail zero-one law, de Finetti for the rows and columns of an array, and the *easy* direction of Aldous–Hoover (every measurable coding of the canonical noise is exchangeable, and every global-free coding is dissociated). What is missing is the representation direction itself: the header of `Arrays/AldousHoover/Basic.lean` states that constructing the coding function from an exchangeable array is still to do, and no such theorem exists in the baseline.

duplicates.note: That layer proves the graph-law case of the same array representation — exchangeable graph laws are graphon mixtures, with dissociated laws as the extreme points (Diaconis–Janson) — which is the `{0,1}`-valued symmetric-array instance of the Aldous–Hoover target here.
Its sampling laws and consistency under label injections restate, for graphs, the finite-population sampling API this layer builds for sequences.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistribut.summary: Tau Ceti has built almost all of this roadmap. Layers 0 to 4 are complete and sorry-free: the `HasPDF`/`rnDeriv` connections for Mathlib's six continuous families, the uniform law on an interval with its whole transform API, the missing elementary theory of every existing family (means, variances, exact `integrableExpSet` domains, mgf/cgf/characteristic functions, convolutions, memorylessness, Gaussian central and absolute moments) and the probability generating function with coefficient recovery, the incomplete gamma and beta functions and the error function with the closed-form Gaussian, gamma, beta, binomial-tail and Poisson-tail cdfs, all nine new scalar families of Layer 3 including their boundary branches, and the classical relationships of Layer 4. Layer 5 is complete apart from one item: the Dirichlet chart density is not proved, though the Dirichlet law, its marginals, aggregation and moments are. Layer 6 has the hardest infrastructure done — the symmetric-matrix carrier with `symmetricLebesgue`, the congruence and Cholesky changes of variables, the multivariate Gamma integral — and the whole Gaussian-Gram Wishart family with its transforms and moments; what is genuinely missing there is the nonsingular real-degree density family `nonsingularWishartMeasure`, and with it the Bartlett decomposition and the inverse-Wishart law.

targets.target: Connect Mathlib's continuous families to `HasPDF` through a single `withDensity` helper
targets.note: The shared helper exists and all six families (gamma, Gaussian, beta, exponential, Cauchy, Pareto) get `HasPDF` plus the identification of `pdf` with the family's pdf, with the `v ≠ 0` / `γ ≠ 0` nondegeneracy hypotheses the layer prescribes.

targets.target: Identify the Radon–Nikodym derivatives of the five `withDensity` families, and the `γ = 0` Cauchy boundary
targets.note: All five are proved, together with the degenerate `cauchyMeasure x₀ 0 = dirac x₀` case; the Gaussian one is taken from Mathlib's `rnDeriv_gaussianReal` as the layer directs.

targets.target: The uniform measure on an interval as `cond volume (Ioc a b)`, with pdf, cdf, mean, variance, mgf, cgf, characteristic function, affine identity and `pdf.IsUniform` bridge
targets.note: `Uniform.lean` carries the whole list, including `uniformPDFReal`, `hasPDF_of_hasLaw_uniformMeasure`, `rnDeriv_uniformMeasure`, `integral_id_uniformMeasure` `= (a+b)/2`, `integrableExpSet_id_uniformMeasure = univ`, the `t = 0` splits of the mgf/cgf/charFun, and `isUniform_of_hasLaw_uniformMeasure`, defined by `cond` exactly so that bridge is definitional.

targets.target: Parameter measurability for Mathlib's existing families, including `Measurable fun r : ℝ≥0 => poissonMeasure r`
targets.note: `Distributions/Measurability.lean` proves it uniformly from joint measurability of the pdfs for the `withDensity` families and separately for the discrete ones; the Poisson case is the one the Layer 4 Gamma-mixed Poisson kernel needs.

targets.target: Bernoulli and binomial: mean, variance, mgf, cgf, characteristic function, convolution and the i.i.d.-Bernoulli-sum law
targets.note: Mathlib supplies the mean; Tau Ceti's `Binomial/Basic.lean` supplies the variance, transforms and the native convolution `binomial n p ∗ binomial m p = binomial (n+m) p`.

targets.target: Geometric: the `p = 0` Dirac boundary, mean, variance, exact mgf domain, mgf, cgf, characteristic function, cumulative mass and memorylessness
targets.note: `Geometric.lean` carries both branches: every transform is proved for `p ≠ 0` and again at `p = 0`, and memorylessness appears both in the division-free form and as `geometricMeasure_cond_Ici`.

targets.target: Poisson: mean, variance, `integrableExpSet = univ`, mgf, cgf
targets.note: On the cast law `(poissonMeasure r).map Nat.cast`, exactly as the layer specifies; the cdf comes from the Layer 2 tail identity.

targets.target: Exponential: mean, variance, exact mgf domain `Iio r`, mgf, cgf, characteristic function, memorylessness, and the minimum of two independent exponentials
targets.note: The roadmap's `map_min_expMeasure` is `hasLaw_min_expMeasure_of_indepFun`, in the `HasLaw`/`IndepFun` form the layer asks for.

targets.target: Gamma: mean, variance, exact mgf domain, mgf, characteristic function, convolution and the scaling law
targets.note: All six items, with the principal `Complex.cpow` in the characteristic function; the roadmap's `map_const_mul_gammaMeasure` is `gammaMeasure_map_const_mul`.

targets.target: Beta: mean, variance, raw moments in terms of `Real.Gamma`, and `integrableExpSet = univ`
targets.note: Exactly the four targets; no mgf/characteristic-function formula is claimed, as the layer directs.

targets.target: Cauchy: characteristic function, cdf, `integrableExpSet = {0}`, non-integrability, the `γ = 0` Dirac formulas, and stability of the family under averaging
targets.note: Both branches are done, and the sample-mean stability theorem is stated for `X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ` with `iIndepFun` and a common law, as specified.

targets.target: Pareto: mean and variance in their exact parameter ranges with matching non-integrability, cdf, and `integrableExpSet = Iic 0`
targets.note: Tau Ceti extends Mathlib's `Pareto` file in the `ProbabilityTheory` namespace, with the `1 < r` / `r ≤ 1` and `2 < r` / `r ≤ 2` splits the layer requires.

targets.target: Real Gaussian: even central moments, vanishing odd central moments, and the absolute central moments
targets.note: The roadmap's `centralMoment_two_mul_gaussianReal` is `centralMoment_id_two_mul_gaussianReal`; the absolute-moment formula with `Real.Gamma ((n+1)/2) / √π` is `integral_abs_sub_pow_gaussianReal`.

targets.target: Probability generating functions: `pgf`, the mgf bridge, multiplicativity over independent sums, the four family formulas, coefficient recovery and `measure_eq_of_pgf_eqOn`
targets.note: `GeneratingFunction.lean` fills the named Mathlib undergraduate gap, including the binomial and geometric pgfs and the negative-binomial one in `NegativeBinomial/Basic.lean`; multiplicativity is stated with the `|t| ≤ 1` and integrability hypotheses the layer insists on rather than unrestricted.

targets.target: Lower incomplete gamma and the regularized gamma function, with convergence, continuity, monotonicity, the recurrence, the limit at infinity and the derivative
targets.note: Defined with the roadmap's exact `if 0 < s then … else 0` convention in `Analysis/SpecialFunctions/IncompleteGamma.lean`, with the analytic API in the same file.

targets.target: The regularized incomplete beta function with its boundary conventions, reflection formula and unit-step recurrence
targets.note: Including the deliberate `regularizedIncompleteBeta 0 b x = 1` convention for `0 < b`, `0 ≤ x` that makes the `m = 0` binomial tail work without a case split.

targets.target: The real error function `Real.erf` and `Real.erfc`, with oddness, monotonicity, limits, derivative and the link to `regularizedGamma (1/2)`
targets.note: In `Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Erf.lean`, following the naming of the Mathlib PR the layer cites.

targets.target: Closed-form cdfs: Gaussian (both branches), gamma, beta, the binomial tail and the Poisson tail
targets.note: All five, plus `poissonMeasure_tail_eq_regularizedGamma`, with the literal roadmap names.

targets.target: Laplace: definition, `b ≤ 0` zero branch, mean, variance, cdf, exact mgf domain, mgf, cgf, characteristic function
targets.note: The whole shared API is present in `Distributions/Laplace.lean`.

targets.target: Log-normal: pushforward definition, density, cdf, `integrableExpSet = Iic 0`, the `v = 0` Dirac branch and the raw moments
targets.note: Defined as `(gaussianReal μ v).map exp`, with the density derived rather than assumed, as the layer requires.

targets.target: Weibull: definition, density, cdf, moments, variance and the three mgf regimes
targets.note: The `1 < k` regime is proved as a convergent series, the `k = 1` regime as the exponential mgf, and `Weibull/Transforms.lean` separates the three cases exactly as the layer demands.

targets.target: Chi-squared: the three-branch definition, the gamma bridge, the full transform API, the `k = 0` Dirac branch and additivity
targets.note: `chiSquaredMeasure_two` is the layer's own completion check `chiSquaredMeasure 2 = expMeasure (1/2)`.

targets.target: Inverse-gamma: definition as the pushforward under inversion, density, cdf, mean and variance in their ranges with matching non-integrability, and `integrableExpSet = Iic 0`
targets.note: All items, including the `0 < a ≤ 1` and `0 < a ≤ 2` non-integrability statements.

targets.target: Student's t: definition, mean/variance in their ranges with matching non-integrability, the cdf in terms of the regularized incomplete beta, and `integrableExpSet = {0}`
targets.note: `studentTMeasure_one` is the layer's completion check `studentTMeasure 1 = cauchyMeasure 0 1`.
